facts.statement: Ratchasimasaurus is a genus of iguanodontian ornithopod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Ratchasimasaurus (meaning "Nakhon Ratchasima lizard") is a genus of iguanodontian ornithopod dinosaur

facts.statement: The only known species, R. suranareae, is named after the 19th-century war heroine Thao Suranari.
facts.quote: The type and only species is R. suranareae, named after Thao Suranari, a 19th-century war heroine.

facts.statement: The genus was named in 2011 by Shibata, Jintasakul, and Azuma.
facts.quote: The genus was named in 2011 by Shibata, Jintasakul & Azuma.

facts.statement: The holotype is housed at the Northeastern Research Institute of Petrified Wood and Mineral Resources, while a mounted skeleton is displayed in River City, Bangkok.
facts.quote: The holotype is currently housed in The Northeastern Research Institute of Petrified Wood and Mineral Resources (NRIPM) and a mounted skeleton exists in River City, Bangkok.

facts.statement: A unique characteristic of Ratchasimasaurus is its elongated and flat dentary ramus.
facts.quote: One autapomorphy (unique characteristic) of Ratchasimasaurus is its elongated and flat ramus of the dentary.

facts.statement: The dentary of the holotype measures 198.1 mm in length.
facts.quote: The length of the dentary is 198.1 mm.

facts.statement: Ratchasimasaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous (Aptian stage) in the Khok Kruat Formation of Nakhon Ratchasima province, northeastern Thailand.
facts.quote: from Early Cretaceous (Aptian stage) Khok Kruat Formation of Nakhon Ratchasima province in northeastern Thailand.

facts.statement: The dinosaur lived in the middle of the Cretaceous period, approximately between 120 and 113 million years ago, from the Aptian to the Albian stages.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 120 a 113 millones de años, desde el Aptiense al Albiense

facts.statement: Ratchasimasaurus is classified within the family Iguanodontidae.
The parent group for Ratchasimasaurus is Hadrosauroidea.
Ratchasimasaurus is diagnosed with characters that are widespread among Styracosterna.
facts.quote: It was considered by one study to be a nomen dubium, diagnosed with characters widespread in Styracosterna.

facts.statement: Ratchasimasaurus exhibits both primitive and derived Iguanodontian characters, including a caudally inclined coronoid process and a derived buccal shelf.
facts.quote: Ratchasimasaurus shows both primitive and derived characters for Iguanodontia, such as "a caudally inclined coronoid process and alveolar trough with a primitive crown impression, and a derived buccal shelf between the tooth row and the coronoid process".

rejected.statement: One study considered Ratchasimasaurus to be a nomen dubium due to its widespread diagnostic characters.
rejected.quote: It was considered by one study to be a nomen dubium, diagnosed with characters widespread in Styracosterna.
